summary: This node derives the reconciliation and evaluation-design layer for the parent. The disagreement between Du et al. 2023 (debate gains) and Smit/Zhang (nulls/boundary conditions) is reconciled by three design inferences: (1) task-type dependence — the gains are not uniform across programming vs. math, so architecture must scope debate to tasks where evidence shows it helps; (2) compute parity — matched-compute comparisons defeat naive debate, so the substrate must be evaluated at equal token/compute budget; and (3) visibility/timing — conformity risk if peer answers are exposed too early, so staged independent commitment is required. Three evaluation-design constraints are added covering the five metric families: (a) quality and diversity/correlation measured as paired pre/post-debate deltas with independence metrics; (b) latency and token cost measured at matched-compute parity per condition; (c) recovery-from-wrong-consensus as a dedicated perturbation test. All six items are explicitly design inferences, informed by, but separated from, source-supported claims.
unresolved: It remains unresolved whether the efficacy of the substrate depends on model heterogeneity, which Zhang proposes as universal antidote (Heter-SoM +6.4%), since this node did not extract the full Zhang analysis.
The exact latency/token accounting rules (e.g., whether to count debate rounds) are not specified in the separator facts and must be fixed by the parent.
